newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Ceteco to issue new shares.
newsitem.headline: Ceteco to issue new shares.

text.p: Trading company and retail group Ceteco Holding NV said on Wednesday it would issue 678,261 non-voting share certificates.
Of the issue, 100,000 share certificates will be taken up by majority stakeholder Hagemeyer, which now owns a 71.6 percent interest in Ceteco.
"The proceeds of the issue will be used to finance further growth of the company," Ceteco said in a statement.
Ceteco said it had granted an option to ABN AMRO Rothschild, as the representative of the banking syndicate, to take up another 86,739 share certificates to cover over-allotments.
If this "green shoe option" is exercised, the total size of the issue will be a maximum of 765,000 share certificates. They will be entitled to the 1997 dividend and payments in later years.
The certificates will be marketed through a book building procedure to institutional and private investors on April 10 and April 11.
Ceteco earlier posted a 1996 net profit of 28.1 million guilders, up from 25.1 million in the previous year. It said it expected a further profit rise in 1997.
The company is mainly active in Latin America, where it has retail chains in various countries.
Hong Kong's First Pacific Co has a controlling stake in Ceteco's parent company Hagemeyer.
